themes_detail.label: Abandoned vehicles surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints spiked to 14 this week, up 144% from the 5.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a rapid deterioration in street conditions that may indicate organized dumping or enforcement gaps.
evidence: 14 abandoned vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (144% spike, z-score 3.32)
Pattern emerged suddenly with no evidence of long-term escalation in prior baseline data
Spike concentrated in single week suggests discrete event (dumping operation, enforcement lapse, or reporting surge)
reporting_angles: Are NYPD and DSNY coordinating on abandoned vehicle removal, or is backlog growing?
Interview residents on specific blocks experiencing the spike to identify geographic concentration and possible dumping hub

themes_detail.label: Tree damage and overgrowth epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree/branch complaints exploded to 15 last week (2300% above 8-week average of 0.6 per week) and illegal tree damage jumped to 8 complaints (300% above baseline), together pointing to either storm damage, deferred Parks maintenance, or organized tree vandalism in Crown Heights.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches: 15 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 20.65, highest severity rating)
Illegal tree damage: 8 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 3.79)
Both spikes occurred in same reporting period, suggesting common cause (weather event, maintenance failure, or coordinated vandalism)
reporting_angles: Did a storm or weather event trigger tree damage in Prospect Park or street canopy last week? Obtain Parks Department incident reports.
Interview Parks Department on tree maintenance schedules and staffing in CD 308; compare complaint clusters to specific parks or blocks
Talk to residents on affected blocks about safety concerns (falling branches, blocked sightlines)

themes_detail.label: Street sign disappearances
themes_detail.summary: Street sign–missing complaints hit 3 this week, a 700% increase over the 0.4 weekly average, alongside a 2300% spike in overgrown tree complaints, suggesting either a focused vandalism campaign or Parks/DOT response lag in a specific zone.
evidence: 3 street sign–missing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Temporally aligned with tree damage spike, suggesting possible single incident or localized infrastructure failure
Low absolute volume but extreme statistical deviation indicates anomalous event rather than seasonal trend
reporting_angles: Map the 3 complaints geographically—are they clustered on specific streets or blocks suggesting targeted vandalism?
Confirm with DOT whether there is a known sign replacement backlog or recent infrastructure damage in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights

themes_detail.label: Homeless assistance requests spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 26 two weeks ago, a 670% increase over the 3.4-complaint weekly average, indicating either a concentrated encampment emergence or crisis event, and aligning with recurring city budget requests for homeless facilities.
evidence: 26 homeless person assistance complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.4 weekly average (670% spike, z-score 13.68)
Community Board has repeatedly requested expansion of homeless facilities funding from Department of Homeless Services, suggesting chronic underresourcing
Spike suggests acute event (new encampment, shelter closure, outreach failure) rather than gradual drift
reporting_angles: Identify the location(s) of the 26 complaints—are they concentrated in a specific park, transit hub, or commercial corridor?
Interview DHS on whether a shelter closed, reduced capacity, or whether a new unsheltered population emerged in the district
Talk to local advocates and residents about conditions; photograph encampments if safe to do so

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk collapse and pedestrian hazards
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints doubled to 14 two weeks ago, up 149% from the 5.6-complaint weekly average, overlapping with a dead animal spike and indicating broader street-level infrastructure decay that may create pedestrian safety issues.
evidence: 14 sidewalk condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 5.6 weekly average (149% spike, z-score 3.5)
Dead animal complaints also spiked to 6 two weeks ago (300% above 1.5 baseline), suggesting broader environmental degradation
High severity rating indicates conditions affecting pedestrian safety and accessibility
reporting_angles: Map sidewalk complaints to identify worst blocks; obtain DOT repair backlog data for Crown Heights
Interview residents with mobility challenges (elderly, wheelchair users) on how poor sidewalk conditions affect daily life
Check whether sidewalk repairs are deferred due to budget constraints or contractor availability
